kai: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in nightly profiler runs after we bumped the NVIDIA driver to 535.54 and switched to nsys 2023.4.
monica: Oof. What does the trace show?
kai: Kernel timeline looks weird — lots of tiny kernels attributed to user space instead of cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels. Spike in host->device memcpy latency too.
raj: Could be missing CUPTI callbacks. We've seen older nsys versions fail to stitch kernels when driver+CUpti mismatch.
sara: I grabbed an nsys report: attached snippet below. The NVTX markers are all there but kernel names are generic `void*` or `cupti-unresolved`.
perf-bot: automated check: regression detected in seq-latency test A (p95 increased from 22ms -> 41ms).
kai: Example excerpt from the timeline (copied):
```
# Timeline slice
[GPU] memcpyHtoD (2.1ms)
[GPU] <unknown kernel> (0.3ms)
[GPU] <unknown kernel> (0.7ms)
[GPU] cublasGemm (1.2ms)
```
monica: How reproducible? only in our CI infra or dev machines too?
kai: Repro on devbox with same driver+nsys combo. On an older node with driver 525 + nsys 2022.3 the timeline looks normal.
raj: Two suspects: (1) CUPTI version mismatch, (2) new driver changed symbol export ordering -> nsys can't map addresses to kernels.
sara: Also seeing KV cache miss rate jump in logs around the same time. Missing proper kernel attribution can break our batch/kvcache heuristics because we rely on kernel classification to tune batch sizes.
ops-bot: note: recent GPU node images rolled out 2026-01-12 with driver 535.54 in prod.
monica: Could the driver cause different launch parameters (grid/block) that make small kernels more frequent? Or is it strictly metadata mapping?
raj: Likely metadata. CUPTI provides activity records; when CUPTI API returns CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL_RECORD with truncated function name, nsys falls back to address-only entries. If that happens, our profiler parsing script labels them as `<unresolved>` and we lose hotpath attribution.
kai: I ran a perfetto capture too — perfetto shows correct GPU names but stack sampling doesn't include CUDA driver frames (no cuBLAS symbols).
sara: Any permission issues? We had a case where container sandbox prevented CUPTI from collecting resource usage.
raj: Good point — check /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope and kcore access; but both devbox and CI had same kernel settings. Also tried running `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt` as root — same unresolved names.
monica: Can you paste the exact nsys + driver combo used?
kai: nsys 2023.4.0, CUDA toolkit 12.2, driver 535.54, CUPTI shipped with toolkit 12.2.
monica: On older working setup: nsys 2022.3.1, driver 525.89, toolkit 12.1.
raj: Action plan: (A) try nsys 2022.x on new driver to see if nsys->driver mismatch is the issue, (B) capture CUPTI event logs with verbosity, (C) try a tiny repro that calls cuBLAS and NVTX markers to see mapping.
sara: I'll run A and C on a spare node. Kai — can you dump a full nsys export (.qdrep) and upload to /tmp/prof-1818123456.qdrep?
kai: Uploaded to s3://redwood-profiles/1818123456/ and added link in the ticket.
ops-bot: reminder: collect node kernel + module versions (uname -a; nvidia-smi --query).
kai: Pasted outputs in the thread: `Linux testnode 6.4.12 ...`, `nvidia-smi 535.54.03`, `cupti-lib 12.2.0`
raj: If A fails, try new nsys build from NVIDIA nightly (they sometimes fix CUPTI mapping regressions). Also check `nsys export --nvtx` behavior.
monica: Another angle — our parsing logic ignores address-only kernels by default. We could heuristically map addresses back to symbols using `cuobjdump --dump-elf` to extract kernel names from cubin and correlate. That would be a fallback for unresolved entries.
sara: I'm on it. I'll also run batch replay with and without the unresolved-kernel fallback and report p95.
kai: Quick workaround: pin driver back to 525 in staging for now to avoid customer impact. Can we do that?
ops-bot: deployment note created: #INC-2984 rollback GPU drivers on staging.
raj: Longer-term we need robust stitching: 1) better CUPTI version checks in our profiler, 2) a fallback symbol resolution step, 3) add instrumentation to the runtime to tag kernels with NVTX + function-id pairs to avoid relying purely on CUPTI.
monica: Agreed. Add a ticket to eng-runtime backlog for the runtime NVTX tag feature and perf parsing fallback.
kai: Thanks everyone. Sara — ping when you have the comparison numbers and the temporary rollback is scheduled. :thumbsup:
sara: Will do. Starting the runs now. :coffee:
